hero.title: Time and Work
hero.description: Time and Work is a critical quantitative aptitude topic frequently tested in the Allahabad High Court RO/ARO and UPPSC examinations. It evaluates a candidate's ability to logically analyze efficiency, rates of working, and fractional contributions of labor over specific durations.

mnemonics.title: Time and Work Mnemonics & Study Tricks

items.title: LET (LCM Efficiency Time)
items.phrase: LCM Gives Efficiency Times Total Work
items.decryption: L = LCM of days, E = Efficiency units, T = Total Work. Remember: Total Work = Efficiency × Time.

items.title: MDH Formula Mnemonic
items.phrase: Many Dogs Howl, While Working Downstairs
items.decryption: M = Men (M₁), D = Days (D₁), H = Hours (H₁) over Work (W₁) equals the second set on the other side.

flashcards.title: Active Recall Flashcards
flashcards.description: Hover or click to reveal the answers. Revisit these cards to build instant recall.

items.question: If A can do a work in 10 days and B in 15 days, what is the total work using the LCM method?
items.answer: 30 units (LCM of 10 and 15). A's efficiency = 3 units/day, B's efficiency = 2 units/day.

items.question: How are wages divided among workers of varying efficiencies working together for the same duration?
items.answer: In the direct ratio of their individual daily efficiencies.

items.question: What is the net work done per hour if an inlet pipe fills a tank in 4 hours and a leak empties it in 12 hours?
items.answer: Net 1/4 - 1/12 = 2/12 = 1/6th of the tank per hour (filling mode).

items.question: If 12 men complete a work in 20 days, how many days will 15 men take?

traps.title: Common Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Inverse Ratio Mistake in Wages: Aspirants often divide wages in the inverse ratio of time taken. Wages must always be distributed according to the ratio of work done or efficiency, which is direct.

Confusing Alternate Day Cycles: In alternate day questions, simply dividing total work by combined efficiency fails when the last block doesn't cleanly divide. Always trace the exact day-by-day progress near completion.
Ignoring Negative Sign for Outlets: When solving pipe and cistern problems, forgetting to assign a negative sign to the outlet or leak rate leads to addition instead of subtraction of units.

deepDive.title: Time and Work Core Study Notes
deepDive.description: Time and Work is a critical quantitative aptitude topic frequently tested in the Allahabad High Court RO/ARO and UPPSC examinations. It evaluates a candidate's ability to logically analyze efficiency, rates of working, and fractional contributions of labor over specific durations.

sections.title: Fundamental Concepts of Time and Work
sections.content:
Understanding the inverse relationship between time taken and efficiency is vital for solving basic and advanced problems.

  • Work-Time Inverse Proportion: If a person completes a piece of work in 'n' days, the work done by that person in 1 day is 1/n part of the total work.
  • Efficiency and Time Relation: Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken. If Person A is twice as efficient as Person B, A takes half the time B takes to complete the same work.
  • Total Work Equation: Total Work = Efficiency (Rate) × Time. In unit terms, it is measured in Man-Days or total units of work derived from LCM.
  • Combined Work Rate: If A can do a work in 'x' days and B in 'y' days, together they can finish it in (x × y) / (x + y) days.

sections.title: Advanced Methods: LCM and Pipe-Cistern
sections.content:
Applying the LCM method eliminates fractions, reducing calculation errors significantly in competitive examinations.

  • LCM Method Principle: Assume total work to be the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the given individual days, and calculate per-day unit efficiency for each entity.
  • Alternate Day Working: When workers take turns alternatively, calculate the cumulative work done in a complete cycle of turns before determining the remaining units.
  • Pipes and Cisterns Correlation: Inlets are treated as positive work rates (efficiency), while outlets or leaks are treated as negative work rates.
  • Negative Work / Leakage Formula: If inlet fills in 'x' hours and outlet empties in 'y' hours (y > x), net time to fill is (x × y) / (y - x) hours.

sections.title: Chain Rule and M-D-H Concepts
sections.content:
The Chain Rule extends time-work principles to handle variables like number of workers, daily working hours, and fraction of work completed.

  • General Formula (M-D-H): (M₁ × D₁ × H₁ × E₁) / W₁ = (M₂ × D₂ × H₂ × E₂) / W₂, where M=Men, D=Days, H=Hours, E=Efficiency, and W=Work.
  • Constant Parameters: If hours or efficiency are not mentioned, they are treated as equal and omitted from both sides of the equation.
  • Work Placement in Formula: Always place the actual work done (or units produced, trenches dug) in the denominator (W₁ and W₂).
  • Proportionate Wages: Wages are always distributed among workers in the ratio of their individual efficiency or daily work done, not time taken.
